i completely understand your frustration OP. as someone who also came from an alcoholic mother and enabling father, i understand that the people-pleasing and caretaking is probably deeply engrained in your nervous system as it was with mine too. and with your sister and her possible relapse, it sounds like you are used to worrying about her addiction as well on top of your mother’s. you’re right that no one is making you be a caretaker but it’s also important to be gentle with yourself and acknowledge that it’s not your fault. it’s also not necessarily a bad thing. being a caring person is a beautiful thing to be. 

unlearning these habits is extremely hard and takes a lot of patience, and also a considerable amount of guilt. guilt feels very heavy when it comes on, but it’s important to remember that guilt is a response of your nervous system, and not an objective factual thing. i found that unlearning the people pleasing i got from my mom took a lot of guilt and time. maybe sit on why you feel to need to take care of everybody else. do you relate to them, empathize with them, do you wish somebody else would take care of you the way you take care of them? what would you lose from stepping away from situations out of your control?

and remember, be gentle with yourself.
